component.name: TV Remote
component.summary: Control an Android TV or Google TV over the network

description.p: TV Remote is a modern GNOME application that lets you control your Android TV from your Linux desktop. It discovers Android TV devices on your local network, pairs with them using the same remote protocol as the Google TV phone app, and provides an intuitive remote control interface.

ul.li: Automatic network scanning to discover Android TV devices
No developer options or ADB needed: pair once with the code shown on the TV
Full D-pad navigation, volume controls, and media buttons
Keyboard shortcuts for all remote functions
Text input for searching and typing on your TV
Auto-connect to last used device on startup
Native GNOME/Libadwaita design following HIG

description.p: Setup: Make sure the TV and this computer are on the same network, then connect and type the pairing code that appears on the TV.
This update focuses on stability and architecture support:

ul.li: Implemented 100% architecture-agnostic execution by removing dependency on native ADB binary
Refactored scrcpy controller to use direct ADB multiplexed stream for input injection
Fixed scrcpy-server connection persistence issues when restarting the app
Improved reliability of device discovery and connection management
Full support for both x86_64 and aarch64 (ARM) platforms

description.p: Major feature update including UI overhaul and new remote capabilities:

ul.li: Added start/end buttons for media playback
Implemented long-press support for buttons and keyboard shortcuts
Added hold-to-repeat for D-pad navigation with mouse
Added refresh button and network scanning to device selection dialog
Improved connection management with device name and model display
Refresh volume state correctly on connection
Modernized "Now Playing" interface and overall UI improvements
Various bug fixes including mute button state and volume slider initialization

description.p: Stable release with improved features and UI enhancements:

ul.li: Added new remote actions: Previous Track, Next Track, Google Assistant, and Captions/Subtitles
Added support for YouTube Rewind shortcut
Refined user interface with more compact and modern button designs
Improved overall visual aesthetics and premium feel
Enhanced keyboard shortcut support
Various bug fixes and performance improvements
